name: Lazarus Shade — Thermal Phantom Injector
description:
The Lazarus Shade is a subcutaneous thermal management system produced by Lazarus Pharmaceuticals in conjunction with a hardware subsidiary, combining a short-duration pharmaceutical agent with a network of implanted micro-radiator filaments to give the user precise, real-time control over their surface thermal emission profile. The pharmaceutical component — administered via autoinjector pen, with effects lasting 90 to 120 minutes — suppresses the body's normal thermoregulatory responses and hands control to the hardware layer. The implanted filament network, a one-time installation procedure taking roughly two hours, can then redistribute, suppress, or selectively emit heat across different body regions under software direction.

The system's most operationally significant capability is thermal impersonation: by studying a target environment's expected thermal signatures — a maintenance worker, a security guard, ambient machinery — the Shade's control software can configure the wearer's emission profile to approximate that signature. On standard thermal imaging, the operator reads not as a concealed intruder but as an expected, boring heat source. The pharmaceutical suppression component also drops the wearer's core temperature output by approximately 2.1°C for the duration, providing baseline thermal reduction even when active impersonation is not engaged.

The Shade carries genuine medical risk. The pharmaceutical component stresses cardiac and thermoregulatory systems, and use more than twice within a 48-hour window without medical supervision has caused fatalities in field conditions. Lazarus Pharmaceuticals sells the pharmaceutical element separately through a prescription pathway nominally intended for 'hyperthermia management therapy,' a fiction that has generated significant regulatory friction and at least two ongoing administrative investigations in GLMZ's health oversight bodies.

cultural_context: The Shade occupies a grim niche in GLMZ's underground. The people who use it regularly know they're trading years off their life for operational capability, and that awareness creates a particular kind of fatalism among habitual users. There's a dark professional humor around 'shade-burners' — operators who have used it so many times that their cardiac profiles are already flagged in Lazarus's own patient data, which Lazarus sells to health insurers. The company's involvement in creating a tool that generates long-term customers for its pharmaceutical division is a darkly noted irony that no one in a position to act on it seems particularly motivated to address.
known_users: deep-cover agents with no extraction timeline
story_hooks: A player's contact is found dead with signs of thermoregulatory collapse — a Shade overdose. But the contact wasn't an operator; they had no reason to be running thermal suppression. Someone dosed them.

Lazarus Pharmaceuticals approaches the players to recover a stolen batch of the Shade's pharmaceutical component — 200 doses, enough to run a significant operation or kill a significant number of people if misused. They're not asking who took it. They just want it back.

A thermal anomaly captured on a facility's security recording shows a signature that doesn't match any employee or expected heat source — it matches a dead woman, a former operator, whose thermal profile is on file from a previous incident. Either someone is impersonating a dead person's heat signature or something else entirely is happening.
